reason: The cited evidence (E1) only describes the layered oxide structure formed on CoCrFeMnNi at 400°C under a single oxygen pressure, with no data on wear, friction, or the effect of varying oxygen partial pressure. It does not support the key premises that an optimal oxide scale reduces wear, that oxygen partial pressure can tailor it for wear resistance, or that the scale is nanocrystalline and self-healing during room-temperature wear.
premises: Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi forms a layered oxide scale with specific elemental distributions (Ni-rich bottom, Cr-rich middle, Fe/Mn/Co-rich outer) under controlled oxidation.
The oxide scale can be nanocrystalline and continuous.
An optimal oxide scale thickness and composition minimizes friction and wear.
Oxygen partial pressure can be used to tailor the oxide scale properties in situ during wear.
Element-specific oxidation kinetics enable self-healing and load-spreading characteristics.
